scenes.title: Two-compartment shuttle box with low center hurdle where the Escapable porcelain dog hops cleanly across while the Yoked case lies still
scenes.era: 1967, University of Pennsylvania behavioral psychology laboratory, Philadelphia

layout.description: High-key 1967 university laboratory showing a clean two-compartment acrylic-and-wood shuttle box divided down the middle by a low shoulder-high barrier with an overhead signal lamp indicating the safe right side.

positions.who: Articulated matte-white porcelain dog sculpture (Escapable Group 1)
positions.where: bounding effortlessly in a clean arc over the low wooden center hurdle into the brightly lit safe right compartment

positions.who: Martin Seligman & Steven Maier (mannequins in 1967 collared shirts, ties, and white lab coats)
positions.where: standing beside the triadic yoked circuit diagram comparing the 90% escape curve against the 67% passive tally

props.name: two-sided shuttle box with low center barrier
props.period_detail: clean white-and-oak test chamber split by an easily stepped-over 15-inch divider
props.physical_behavior: overhead lamp switches off the instant the porcelain sculpture clears the low hurdle

props.name: triadic yoked nose-panel console
props.period_detail: side bench showing two identical circular nose panels — Panel A wired LIVE and Panel B wired YOKED (passive)
props.physical_behavior: proves both groups received identical timing the day before

props.name: escape latency tally chart
props.period_detail: 1967 clipboard graph contrasting Group 1 (fast jump) vs Group 2 (two-thirds failure to cross)
props.physical_behavior: documents that control, not stress duration, governs action

actions.verb_sequence: illuminates on the left side -> Porcelain dog sculpture from Group 1 steps up and bounds cleanly over the low center barrier -> lamp clicks off in two seconds
traces the wire from Live Panel A to Yoked Panel B on the benchtop console

reactions.reaction: stands alert and calm in the safe right compartment
circles the stark behavioral split created by a single working off-switch

scenes.wardrobe: 1967 researchers in crisp white cotton lab coats over Oxford shirts and narrow ties; animal subject strictly rendered as a clean articulated matte-white porcelain dog sculpture.
scenes.recognition_hook: Given the exact same stress duration down to the millisecond the day before, the animal whose button worked leaps the low hurdle in two seconds while its yoked partner never even tries.

key_visual.description: an articulated matte-white porcelain dog leaping cleanly over a low center divider inside a two-compartment 1967 shuttle box beside two lab-coated researchers and a yoked panel console

scenes.title: Yoked twin nose panels: identical clock, opposite control

layout.description: Close tabletop view of two side-by-side circular response panels wired through a shared timer relay.

positions.where: demonstrating how pressing Panel A stops both timers simultaneously while pressing Panel B changes nothing

props.name: shared electromechanical relay timer
props.period_detail: single clock feeding two chambers identically
props.physical_behavior: eliminates physical duration as an explanation

actions.verb_sequence: presses Live Panel A stopping the clock -> presses Dead Panel B showing the clock keeps running

reactions.reaction: records identical cumulative seconds on both counters

scenes.recognition_hook: Wiring both chambers to the exact same clock proved helplessness came from zero control, not extra hardship.

scenes.title: 2016 Boulder neuroscience reversal: vmPFC braking the brainstem
scenes.era: 2016, University of Colorado Boulder neuroscience office

layout.description: Modern sunlit office whiteboard displaying TWO circuit diagrams: '1967 Assumption (Learned Passivity)' crossed out beside '2016 Discovery (Learned vmPFC Control Braking Dorsal Raphe)'.

positions.who: Older Steven Maier & Martin Seligman mannequins
positions.where: standing side-by-side tapping the green inhibitory arrow from vmPFC down to brainstem raphe

props.name: 50-year circuit comparison board
props.physical_behavior: highlights one of psychology's rarest self-reversals

actions.verb_sequence: draws a bold top-down brake arrow from prefrontal cortex to brainstem raphe

reactions.reaction: nods warmly embracing the fifty-year correction

scenes.wardrobe: Modern tailored blazers and open-collar shirts.
scenes.recognition_hook: Fifty years later, the original authors proved passivity is the brainstem default — CONTROL is what the frontal lobe learns.

scenes.title: Rebuilding agency with a concrete 5-minute controllable win

layout.description: Sunlit desk where an overwhelmed worker sets aside a massive uncontrollable binder and checks off three concrete 5-minute action cards.

positions.where: sliding a crisp completed card into a 'Done' tray

props.name: three small 'In My Control' index cards
props.period_detail: tangible micro-actions with immediate visible feedback

actions.verb_sequence: completes first 5-minute action -> checks card -> stands up energized for the next step

reactions.reaction: posture lifts out of freeze mode

scenes.recognition_hook: One small action-to-outcome win switches your prefrontal mastery brake back online.
